summary: Backlog features tested end-to-end: (1) server-side rate limiter on socket message:send — MIN_GAP (too-fast), BURST, passthrough, stranger-room applicability, disconnect-clears-bucket; (2) URL query-param sync on sidebar clicks and on direct URL entry (/chat?room=..., /chat?tab=stranger, invalid-room fallback to clean /chat); (3) moderator pagination REST (limit/offset clamping, page disjointness) and UI (mod-pagination testids, prev/next enable/disable, filter change resets page). Also ran regression on all prior backend suites. 42/42 pytest tests pass. All frontend flows verified via Playwright.
critical_code_review_comments: Rate limiter uses in-memory Map keyed by socket.id. On horizontal scale (multiple Node instances behind LB), each instance has independent buckets → a client bouncing between pods effectively gets N× the quota. Acceptable for MVP; document/limit to single-instance deploy or move to Redis if scale-out becomes needed.
checkRateLimit does not add the current timestamp when it rejects, which is correct (rejection should not count towards quota). Good.

Server /api/mod/reports uses `parseInt(...) || 50` for limit — falsy fallback means limit=0 falls back to 50 (arguably unexpected). Similarly limit clamp uses Math.min(200, Math.max(1, ...)) after the || default, so 0 is treated as 'unset'. Consider using Number.isFinite() check for stricter validation, but current behavior is safe (never <1, never >200).

Moderator.jsx computes filterTotal from stats.open/resolved/total. If backend stats include reports that don't match current page slice (e.g., counts across statuses), pagination is still correct. Note that filterTotal derivation happens client-side using the top-level stats object — verified matches server-side counts in this test run.

Chat.jsx uses `useMemo(resolveInitialRoom, [])` (empty deps, disabled lint) which is fine because URL params are only consulted at mount. Good pattern for deep-linking without re-reading params on every render.
Minor: humanReadableRateError falls through with a generic 'Rate limit hit. Try again shortly.' for any unknown rule — safe default.
